description: This topic explains how solids, liquids and gases expand when heated, the particle reasons behind it, the anomalous expansion of water, and the everyday applications and problems of thermal expansion.

mcq.questionText: What is meant by thermal expansion?

options.text: The increase in the size of a body when it is heated
The increase in the mass of a body when it is heated
The decrease in the size of a body when it is cooled only
The change in colour of a body when it is heated

mcq.explanation: Thermal expansion is the increase in the dimensions (length, area or volume) of a substance when its temperature rises.

mcq.questionText: When a solid is heated, why does it expand according to the particle theory?

options.text: The particles increase in size
New particles are created inside the solid
The particles vibrate more and move slightly farther apart
The particles gain extra mass

mcq.explanation: Heating gives particles more kinetic energy so they vibrate harder and occupy slightly more space, increasing the overall size; the particles themselves do not grow.

mcq.questionText: Which state of matter expands the most for the same rise in temperature?

options.text: Solids
Liquids
Gases
They all expand by the same amount

mcq.explanation: Gas particles are far apart with very weak forces between them, so gases expand much more than liquids, which in turn expand more than solids.

mcq.questionText: Why are small gaps left between sections of railway lines?

options.text: To save on the cost of steel
To allow the rails to expand on hot days without bending
To allow rain water to drain away
To make the train run more quietly

mcq.explanation: On hot days the steel rails expand; the gaps give room for this expansion so the rails do not buckle and bend out of shape.

mcq.questionText: A bimetallic strip is made by joining two metals. Why must the two metals be different?

options.text: So that they have different colours
So that they expand by different amounts and the strip bends
So that one metal can conduct electricity and the other cannot
So that the strip becomes heavier

mcq.explanation: Different metals have different rates of expansion, so when heated one side lengthens more than the other and the strip bends.

mcq.questionText: A tight metal lid on a glass jar can often be loosened by running it under hot water. Why does this work?

options.text: The hot water makes the lid slippery only
The metal lid expands more than the glass, loosening its grip
The hot water dissolves the metal lid slightly
The glass jar shrinks in hot water

mcq.explanation: Metals expand more than glass for the same temperature rise, so the heated lid widens more than the jar neck and becomes easier to turn.

mcq.questionText: In a liquid-in-glass thermometer, why does the liquid rise up the tube when the bulb is warmed?

options.text: The liquid is pushed up by air entering the bulb
The glass contracts and squeezes the liquid upward
The liquid expands and is forced up the narrow tube
The liquid turns into a gas and rises

mcq.explanation: Warming the bulb makes the liquid expand; because the tube (capillary) is very narrow, a small increase in volume produces a large, visible rise.

mcq.questionText: Which property makes mercury and coloured alcohol suitable as thermometric liquids?

options.text: They do not expand at all
They expand evenly (uniformly) over a range of temperatures
They are good conductors of electricity
They are heavier than water

mcq.explanation: A good thermometric liquid expands uniformly so that equal temperature changes give equal changes in length along the scale.

mcq.questionText: Between 0 degrees C and 4 degrees C, what happens to water as it is warmed?

options.text: It expands like other liquids
It contracts (its volume decreases)
Its volume stays exactly the same
It immediately turns into ice

mcq.explanation: Water behaves anomalously: as it warms from 0 to 4 degrees C it contracts rather than expands, reaching its smallest volume at 4 degrees C.

mcq.questionText: At what temperature does water have its maximum density?

options.text: 0 degrees C
4 degrees C
100 degrees C
10 degrees C

mcq.explanation: Because water has its smallest volume at 4 degrees C, the same mass occupies the least space there, giving water its maximum density.

mcq.questionText: Why does ice float on water?

options.text: Ice is made of a different substance from water
Ice is less dense than water because water expands on freezing
Ice has more mass than the water it replaces
Ice contains trapped salt

mcq.explanation: Water expands as it freezes, so ice is less dense than liquid water and therefore floats.

mcq.questionText: Electrical overhead and telephone wires are fixed loosely between poles. Why?

options.text: To use more wire and increase the bill
So they do not snap when they contract on cold days
To make the wires look attractive
So that birds can rest on them

mcq.explanation: Wires contract and become shorter in cold weather; leaving them slack prevents them from becoming too tight and snapping.

mcq.questionText: What is the main reason a thick glass cup may crack when boiling water is poured into it suddenly?

options.text: The glass turns into a liquid
The inside expands quickly while the outside is still cool, causing uneven expansion
Boiling water is heavier than the glass
Glass always cracks when it gets wet

mcq.explanation: Glass is a poor conductor, so the inner surface heats and expands faster than the outer surface; this uneven expansion sets up stresses that crack the glass.

mcq.questionText: Concrete roads and bridges are built in sections with gaps between them. These gaps are called expansion joints. What is their purpose?

options.text: To allow water to be stored
To allow the concrete to expand and contract without cracking
To mark the boundary of each section for builders
To reduce the weight of the bridge

mcq.explanation: Concrete expands in heat and contracts in cold; expansion joints give it room to move so the structure does not crack or buckle.

mcq.questionText: A steel bridge expands when heated. To allow for this, one end of the bridge is often placed on rollers. What problem does this prevent?

options.text: It prevents the bridge from rusting
It prevents the bridge from buckling or pushing on its supports as it expands
It prevents vehicles from sliding off
It prevents the bridge from becoming heavier

mcq.explanation: The rollers let the bridge lengthen and shorten freely with temperature changes, avoiding large forces that would buckle the bridge or damage its supports.

fib.questionText: When a substance is heated, its particles gain more _____ energy and vibrate faster.
fib.explanation: Heating increases the kinetic energy of particles, causing them to vibrate more vigorously and move slightly farther apart.

fib.questionText: Of the three states of matter, _____ expand the least for the same rise in temperature.
fib.explanation: Solids have strong forces holding their particles in fixed positions, so they expand the least compared with liquids and gases.

fib.questionText: The strip made by joining two different metals together, used in thermostats, is called a _____ strip.
fib.explanation: A bimetallic strip bends when heated because the two metals expand by different amounts.

fib.questionText: The unusual behaviour of water that causes it to contract between 0 and 4 degrees C is known as the _____ expansion of water.
fib.explanation: Water expands when warmed above 4 degrees C but contracts between 0 and 4 degrees C, an exception called anomalous expansion.

fib.questionText: Water has its maximum density at a temperature of _____ degrees Celsius.
fib.explanation: At 4 degrees C water has its smallest volume and therefore its greatest density.

fib.questionText: Small gaps left between railway lines to allow for expansion are an example of taking a _____ against thermal expansion.
fib.explanation: Engineers take precautions such as expansion gaps to prevent damage caused by expanding materials.

fib.questionText: In a thermometer, the liquid is held in a glass _____ at the bottom which is connected to a very narrow tube.
fib.explanation: The bulb holds the thermometric liquid; when warmed, the liquid expands and rises into the narrow capillary tube.

fib.questionText: When ice forms on a pond, the layer of ice acts as an _____ that keeps the water below from freezing, allowing fish to survive.
fib.explanation: Because of water's anomalous expansion, ice floats on top and insulates the water beneath, so aquatic life can survive winter.

fib.questionText: A liquid generally expands _____ than a solid for the same temperature rise.
fib.explanation: Liquid particles are held by weaker forces than solid particles, so liquids expand more than solids.

fib.questionText: When water freezes into ice it _____ in volume, which is why bottles of water can burst in a freezer.
fib.explanation: Unlike most substances, water expands on freezing, so the increasing volume can break a sealed container.

tf.questionText: All substances expand when they are heated and contract when they are cooled.
tf.explanation: Most substances behave this way, but water between 0 and 4 degrees C is an exception, contracting as it is warmed.

tf.questionText: Gases expand more than liquids and solids for the same rise in temperature.
tf.explanation: Gas particles are far apart with very weak forces, so gases show the greatest expansion.

tf.questionText: When a solid expands on heating, its individual particles become larger.
tf.explanation: The particles do not grow; they vibrate more and move slightly farther apart, increasing the overall size of the solid.

tf.questionText: A bimetallic strip bends when heated because the two metals expand by different amounts.
tf.explanation: The metal that expands more forms the outer curve of the bend, making the strip curve toward the metal that expands less.

tf.questionText: Ice is denser than liquid water, which is why it sinks.
tf.explanation: Ice is less dense than water because water expands on freezing, so ice floats rather than sinks.

tf.questionText: Gaps are left between railway lines to allow the metal rails to expand in hot weather.
tf.explanation: The expansion gaps prevent the rails from buckling when they lengthen on hot days.

tf.questionText: Thermal expansion has no useful applications and only causes problems.
tf.explanation: Thermal expansion is usefully applied in thermometers, thermostats, fitting metal rims on wheels and bimetallic switches.

tf.questionText: A liquid-in-glass thermometer works because the liquid expands more than the glass when heated.
tf.explanation: Since the liquid expands more than the glass, the extra volume is pushed up the narrow tube and shows a temperature reading.

tf.questionText: Water reaches its maximum density at 0 degrees Celsius.
tf.explanation: Water has its maximum density at 4 degrees C, not at 0 degrees C.

tf.questionText: Overhead electric wires are fixed slightly loose so they do not snap when they contract in cold weather.
tf.explanation: Wires shorten as they contract in the cold; the slack prevents them from becoming too tight and breaking.

summary.correctAnswer: The increase in size of a substance when its temperature rises.
summary.explanation: It affects length, area and volume of solids, liquids and gases.

summary.correctAnswer: Heated particles gain kinetic energy, vibrate more and move farther apart.
summary.explanation: The particles stay the same size; only their spacing and motion increase.

summary.questionText: Order of expansion among the states of matter
summary.correctAnswer: Gases expand most, then liquids, and solids expand least.
summary.explanation: Weaker forces between particles allow greater expansion.

summary.correctAnswer: Water contracts between 0 and 4 degrees C, then expands above 4 degrees C.
summary.explanation: This is opposite to the normal behaviour of liquids.

summary.correctAnswer: Water has its maximum density at 4 degrees C.
summary.explanation: At 4 degrees C the same mass of water occupies the least volume.

summary.correctAnswer: Water expands on freezing, making ice less dense than water.
summary.explanation: Less dense ice floats and insulates the water below.

summary.correctAnswer: Two joined metals expand by different amounts, so the strip bends when heated.
summary.explanation: Used in thermostats and fire alarms to make or break circuits.

summary.correctAnswer: Liquid in the bulb expands and rises up a narrow tube to show temperature.
summary.explanation: A good thermometric liquid expands uniformly.

summary.questionText: Common problems caused by thermal expansion
summary.correctAnswer: Buckling rails, cracking glass, sagging or snapping wires and bursting pipes.
summary.explanation: These happen when materials are not given room to expand or contract.

summary.correctAnswer: Leaving expansion gaps in rails, roads and bridges and fixing wires loosely.
summary.explanation: These allow safe expansion and contraction without damage.

hoq.questionText: A bimetallic strip is made of brass and iron, where brass expands more than iron. When the strip is heated, in which direction does it bend?

options.text: It bends so that the brass is on the outside of the curve
It bends so that the iron is on the outside of the curve
It stays perfectly straight
It coils into a complete circle every time

hoq.explanation: The metal that expands more (brass) becomes longer and forms the outer, longer side of the curve, so the strip bends with brass on the outside and iron on the inside.

hoq.questionText: In a deep lake during cold weather, why does water at the very bottom often stay at about 4 degrees C while ice forms on the surface?

options.text: Because the bottom is heated by the ground
Because water at 4 degrees C is densest and sinks to the bottom, while colder, less dense water rises and freezes on top
Because cold water is always heavier than warm water
Because ice sinks and warms the bottom water

hoq.explanation: Owing to the anomalous expansion of water, the densest water (4 degrees C) collects at the bottom, while water cooler than 4 degrees C is less dense, rises, and freezes at the surface, keeping the depths liquid.

hoq.questionText: A metal ball just passes through a metal ring at room temperature. If only the ball is heated strongly, what is observed?

options.text: The ball passes through more easily because metals shrink when heated
The ball no longer passes through because it has expanded and become larger
Nothing changes because heating does not affect size
The ring expands and the ball passes through more easily

hoq.explanation: Heating the ball makes it expand and grow slightly larger, so it can no longer fit through the unheated ring; this classic ball-and-ring experiment demonstrates expansion of solids.
